section: §3 G1(a); §4 Day 1; Week-1 exit gate; §6 risk row 1
issue: G1a is either impossible or circular. The Q1 scorer (barrier_oracle_depth.score) charges every IR node from an operation-level table: the favourable table takes the minimum over all range-specialised f40 leaves, and the representative table takes the median. The recorded 2,972,154 is parallel_source.make_schedule's dependency_only_forward_t_depth, a longest path computed with the actual leaf cost of each compiled call. Rescoring the compiled C4 target with 'the same scorer' therefore cannot reproduce 2,972,154, so a hard Day-1 gate fails by construction. The only way to reproduce it exactly is to feed the scorer the per-node compiled leaf costs. That repeats the same max-plus longest-path computation over the same leaf JSON files, so it validates arithmetic already done by make_schedule and says nothing about the min/median table approximation that C3 and C4 actually use.
evidence: I ran score() on results/controlled_priority_completion/range_compile_v1/C4_f40/target.json (7,639 nodes, output Y_6). Favourable table: 1,818,771 (0.612x the recorded value). Representative table: 3,201,635 (1.077x). Exact per-node leaf costs from source.json forward_calls (1:1 with non-input nodes, out-ids equal): 2,972,154. range_parallel_v1/C4_f40_limit_all.json dependency_only_forward_t_depth = 2972154. Scorer code: barrier_oracle_depth.py leaf_costs() and score(). Dependency-bound code: parallel_source.py make_schedule, arrival[value] = cost + max(arrival[args]). The favourable and representative tables are built from leaves_f40, which holds the leaves of both the C4 and H8 compilations, so a C4 check is in-sample.
fix: Replace G1a with a bracket validation and rename the exact rescoring as a code-consistency check. (i) Consistency: per-node exact rescoring of C4 and H8 equals the recorded 2,972,154 and 3,075,738. (ii) In-sample table check: report favourable/exact = 0.612 and representative/exact = 1.077 for C4, and the same ratios for H8. Gate: favourable <= exact. (iii) Out-of-sample check on the knock-out itself (see the G1b row): score the same optimized IR that is compiled, and compare against make_schedule's dependency_only_forward_t_depth and wave-scheduled t_depth. Gate: favourable score <= compiled dependency-only depth; record the gap factors. Restate C3 as a bracket [favourable-table estimate, compiled per-node depth] rather than a single 'T-depth'.

section: §3 G1(b); §4 Days 1-2; C3 ('certified reversible IR'); §6 risk row 2
issue: The knock-out oracle cannot be emitted through the range-certified path in the time allotted, and the plan does not say which path G1b uses. The favourable and representative tables come from RangedLibrary multipliers. Those leaves are valid only on independently certified operand intervals; the narrowest is a (41,13)-bit multiply at T-depth 11,088. The knock-out IR has no range certificate. The existing certifier cannot produce one without new proof code: ranges_for_compiled is hard-wired to build_finance(model), rejects anything other than f40/q32, and regenerates the compound graph to compare. WitnessGraph supplies the exp_residual lemma only for ir.Graph.exp, but Q1 uses the free function exp_estrin, so the lemma never fires. Emitting through the unranged base library is feasible in about half a day, but it only checks that the compiler wires the leaves correctly. Its depth is trivially larger (each full-width multiply is 90,592 T-depth), so it neither confirms nor refutes the favourable table. C3's word 'certified' is unsupported until a knock-out range certificate exists.
evidence: I ran range_audit.Audit(data, {}) on barrier_oracle_depth.build(4,12): 209 unresolved signed-overflow sites (add 83, shift 78, mul 48). Without witnesses, the widest multiplier operands are (50,41), (49,41), (41,41) and (48,41) bits. ranged_run.py asserts certificate['guaranteed'] and not certificate['signed_overflow_sites'] before it uses RangedLibrary. range_audit.ranges_for_compiled raises 'This certificate is restricted to f40/q32 finance' and compares against optimize(prune(build_finance(model)...)). ranged_multiplier.RangedLibrary leaf 'validity': 'Only on the certified signed operand intervals'. Unranged f40 multiply (results/controlled_completion_followup/arithmetic_v1/leaves_f40): t_depth 90,592, 41,424 CCX. Timing reference: compile_v1 C4 f40 took 31 s including leaf builds; C4 full-source basis executions took 8-35 s each (controlled_source_completion/validation_v2/full_source_basis.json); the Q1 build takes about 1 s.
fix: Split G1b and add half a day or more. G1b-i (Day 2, feasible): optimize() the 4x12 IR, compile_graph it with the unranged arithmetic_v1/leaves_f40 library, and execute at least 16 basis inputs plus edge inputs against ir.evaluate. Report make_schedule dependency-only and wave-scheduled depths. G1b-ii (Days 2-3): subclass WitnessGraph to register the exp_estrin residual witness and the log-mantissa witness through normals_graph. Generalise ranges_for_compiled to accept a builder callable and f. Certify zero overflow sites, compile with RangedLibrary, and replace the operation-level min/median tables with per-node certified leaf costs. Add a unit test of the new lemma and include it in R-B's scope. Until G1b-ii passes, C3 must drop 'certified' and report favourable-table numbers only as a quantum-favourable estimate.

section: §1 C3/C4; §3 G1; barrier_oracle_depth.leaf_costs
issue: The 'favourable' table charges each knock-out node the cheapest leaf of that operation type in a library built for a different graph. That understates the knock-out depth in specific, fixable ways. Every cmul is charged 1,648, which is the cost of a power-of-two constant, yet 6 of the knock-out's 8 distinct cmul constants are not powers of two and cost 34,656-46,176. Every cos lookup (60 nodes on the Box-Muller path) is charged 1,600, the 32-entry log-table cost, instead of 4,096. C3 then presents the favourable number as 'the' clean-call T-depth (8.9-9.0x10^5). The direction favours the quantum side, so the negative decision survives, but a referee will reject a depth figure that is known to undercount by roughly 1.4x.
evidence: leaf_costs() takes min(d for d,_ in v) per operation over range_compile_v1/leaves_f40. The minimum cmul (1,648) has c = +/-2^41 (+/-2.0) and the next cheapest are 2^39, 2^38, ...; the cheapest non-power-of-two cmul in the library is 24,240. The lookup leaves are log 1,600, cos 4,096 and cdf 23,552. I built the knock-out's 8 cmul leaves with primitives.build('cmul',72,40,...) in 2.2 s: t_depth values 46176, 1648, 40976, 34656, 39376, 1696, 36576 and 40848. Rescoring B4x12 Box-Muller with per-constant cmul and per-table lookup costs, keeping multiplies at the favourable 11,088, raises the forward depth from 442,529 to 638,003 (1.44x). With multiplies at the median 40,880 it is 1,025,299.
fix: In G1 (Day 2), replace the operation-level tables with a per-node cost model: cmul by its actual constant (cheap to build), lookup by table, multiply by certified operand widths once G1b-ii exists, and the actual leaf for every other operation. Report three numbers: per-node certified depth, dependency-only compiled depth, and wave-scheduled depth. Keep the favourable table only as an explicitly labelled lower sensitivity. Regenerate C3/C4 from the new JSON and do not hard-code 8.9-9.0x10^5 or 1,138-5,765x in the plan or the ledger before the freeze.

section: §3 G6; §2 assets row 'Earlier f=24/f=40 compilations'; §4 Day 2

section: §3 G3; §1 C4 numbers; barrier_decision.classical_seconds
issue: The archived P3 timing, and therefore T_C and D_max, includes a fixed first-call overhead of about 5 s per worker (JIT or cache load and process start) that is spread across per-point cost. For 4x12 the per-point cost used is 2.8x the marginal cost. G3's 'setup reported separately' does not define which overheads count toward T_C. The overhead favours quantum, so the decision survives, but once warm timing is used C4's '5,765x' for 4x12 roughly doubles. The plan hard-codes C4's '1,138-5,765x' and gates only on 'decision unchanged', so the headline figure is not pinned to post-G3 values.

The marginal cost (t17 - t8)/(2^17 - 2^8) is 2.03e-5 s. For 8x52 the figures are 2.13e-4 against 2.00e-4 (7%). classical_seconds at $0.001 is 5.86 s for 4x12 against about 2.2 s with marginal cost. The CPU is hybrid (Intel Family 6 Model 170, 22 logical CPUs), and 16 workers are spread over P- and E-cores.

section: Week-1 exit gate, bullet 2 ('scored depth equals or bounds the scheduled depth'); §3 G1(b)
issue: The G1b pass criterion is ambiguous in two ways. It does not name which 'scheduled depth' is meant, and it does not say which direction 'bounds' runs. The compiler reports three depths that differ by up to 37x. compile_graph's source.json t_depth is a serial sum of all leaf depths, so any critical-path score is trivially below it. make_schedule reports a dependency-only depth and a realisable wave-scheduled depth, about 2x apart for C4. For a quantum-favourable scorer, the meaningful test is scored <= realisable depth, with the gap reported. 'Equals or bounds' can pass vacuously against the serial number.
evidence: C4 range compile: source.json resources.t_depth = 218,988,506 (clean, schedule 'serial clean leaves ... valid upper bound, not optimal'). range_parallel_v1/C4_f40_limit_all.json: resources.t_depth = 11,609,892 (clean, wave schedule) against 2 x dependency_only_forward_t_depth = 5,944,308 (1.95x). Logical qubits: 635,344 serial, 855,344 for the full-parallel waves. Q1's score() computes only the dependency-only critical path, and Q1 reports no qubit count for its unlimited-parallelism assumption.
fix: Rewrite the gate as follows. For the compiled knock-out, report (a) favourable-table score, (b) per-node score, (c) make_schedule dependency_only_forward_t_depth, (d) wave-scheduled t_depth at parallel_limit None, 128 and 32, and (e) logical qubits at each limit. Pass if (a) <= (b) == (c) <= (d). Carry (d) and (e) into C3 as the realisable figure and into G9's qubit-cap proposition.

issue: G5's formula 'explicit calls / (sigma/e)' is ambiguous by more than an order of magnitude, and it transfers a schedule built for a different estimand. The certified schedules were built for the compound C4/H8 residual Y, with its own second moment, normaliser or span, and a 0.003 failure probability. They also count different units: controlled-U applications versus Grover iterates, each of which contains two source-and-inverse passes. Q in barrier_decision counts clean source calls. Depending on schedule and unit, k_explicit comes out between about 5.5x10^3 and 7x10^4, and none of those values belongs to the knock-out's own normalisation (payoff bounded by (140-100)e^-0.03 = 38.8 against sigma 5.73).
evidence: estimator_hadamard.json: C4 continuous-moment schedule has sum controlled_U_calls 1,203,320 at error 0.00203, moment 0.1945, normalizer 16; H8 has 2,967,610 at moment 1.128. The digital-support-bound variants have 2.70x10^8 and 2.68x10^8. estimator_bounded.json: controlled_grover_calls 7,864,305, source_and_inverse_passes 15,728,610, span 256. Taking sigma = sqrt(moment) gives sigma/e of about 217 (C4) and 508 (H8), so k is about 5,540 (Hadamard, U calls), 36,200 (bounded, Grover iterates) or 72,400 (bounded, source passes).
fix: Define k in G5 as the number of clean source calls (forward plus inverse = one D_call) multiplied by e/sigma for the same estimand, at the same confidence as the classical side (99.5%). Report k_explicit for each certified schedule with its unit conversion. Add a separately labelled 'knock-out transfer' row that recomputes a bounded-QAE schedule for the knock-out's own range and sigma using estimator_bounded's allocation code. Budget half a day or more, not a fraction of Day 4.

issue: The AI-use disclosure is a single Day-9 writing item with no provenance log. Venues require different placement and specific content: model name and version, which sections were AI-generated, the level of use, the reason for use, and use for code or bibliography. Some also encourage keeping prompts and drafts. That cannot be reconstructed accurately after 15 days of multi-agent waves.
evidence: Quantum https://quantum-journal.org/instructions/authors/: disclose 'in the author contribution statement' (examples: 'grammar-checker, reformatting, text production, image production, bibliographic research, production of code or calculations'). Springer/QIP: in the Methods section. IEEE https://open.ieee.org/author-guidelines-for-artificial-intelligence-ai-generated-text/ (search result, not fetched): in the acknowledgments, naming the AI system, the specific sections and the level of use, including code. IOP https://publishingsupport.iopscience.iop.org/questions/generative-ai-tools/ (search result): in the Acknowledgements, with model and version; keep drafts and prompts. section: §7 Author time; §8; Week-3 exit gate
issue: Every venue makes the human authors fully accountable for AI-generated content. The plan budgets about 4 author-hours in total, and nothing in the definition of done shows that the author has checked the G9 proposition and proof, the C1-C7 claims or the AI-written text. A Day-15 manuscript described as ready could therefore not be submitted in good faith.
evidence: APS https://journals.aps.org/prxquantum/authors: 'Authors are fully responsible for accuracy and must review and refine all AI-generated content.' Springer/QIP: 'there must be human accountability for the final version of the text and agreement from the authors that the edits reflect their original work.' fix: Budget realistic author time: at least 1-2 days to read the full text, check the proof and the claim ledger, and sign off. Otherwise state explicitly that Day 15 delivers a draft that still awaits author verification.
